posts.headline: Week 3 Wall: Undefeated Frauds Face Reality Check
posts.body: Jewpacabra and Dicks out for Harambe rode cupcake schedules to 4-0 records—but the gauntlet tightens this week. Meanwhile, The Show's 0-4 mark hides elite execution. We break down who's walking into a buzz saw.
content: Boom—Week 3 is the league-wide reckoning. I'm told the average opponent difficulty spikes to 46 this week, and that's where the pretenders get exposed. Check the Gauntlet rankings, and you'll see Suh girls, one cup and Badd Boys sharing the crown at difficulty 51—both facing an absolute gauntlet for the rest of the season. This is what separates contenders from flash-in-the-pan teams: can you survive when the schedule stops handing you wins?

Here's the spiciest finding: Titsburgh Feelers just became the week's biggest riser, jumping 10 spots as their remaining opponent PPG climbed to 127. Their brutal slate (difficulty 50) is about to get worse. But the real story is the undefeated frauds. League sources tell me Jewpacabra rolled to 4-0 against a laughably soft past difficulty of 23—their record is a mirage. Same with Dicks out for Harambe, who are 4-0 against a past difficulty of 37. Both teams are about to collide with real teams, and their playoff hopes could evaporate fast.

Now flip the narrative: The Show is 0-4 against a brutal past difficulty of 63—the hardest slate anyone has faced so far. Money is nice, but championships are better, and this team's execution has been elite despite the record. Meanwhile, Drunk Indians got massive relief this week, dropping 12 spots in difficulty. After playing through a meat-grinder schedule, they're finally catching breather opponents. The standings don't tell the whole story—strength of schedule does.

The movers are real. Get off my Ditka and No Soup For You caught breaks (down 2 and 7 spots, respectively), while Midwestside Connection and The Show both tightened their belts, moving up 5 and 7. The contrast is stark: some teams are walking downhill the rest of the way, others are climbing Everest. This is why we have the Gauntlet rankings—to separate illusions from truth.

Want to know if your team's season is salvageable or if you need to blow it up? The full dashboard breaks down every team's week-by-week gauntlet at the Gauntlet. The undefeated frauds should be nervous. The winless overachievers should be hopeful. And everyone else? Time to get real about what's ahead.
